title: Interpretation audit identified selection confounds
detail: The first comparison matches 32 examples and optimizer updates, but selected solution lengths and training order differ. Ranked examples are trained in BM25 order while random examples are shuffled. Development question text also contributed to the pre-existing reference index statistics, though development answers and outcomes were not ranking inputs. Report these limits, preserve the frozen run, and avoid claiming that ranking alone caused any difference.

title: First ranked versus random run completed
detail: Numeric development matches out of 16: baseline 13, ranked 13, random 13. Supervised training tokens: ranked 3260, random 2534. Both adapters and raw evaluations saved. One seed and development data only; no final-test or robust generalization claim.

title: Comparison results independently audited
detail: Original Granite, BM25 selected, and random selected each scored 13 of 16. All 48 outputs have plain numeric final answers and no truncation. Ranked fixes one baseline error but introduces another; random has the same correctness pattern as baseline. Ranked used 3260 supervised tokens versus 2534 for random, about 28.65 percent more. No ranking accuracy or fixed-token efficiency advantage is demonstrated. One ambiguous benchmark item is retained under the frozen scoring policy.
